page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Within the column, a heading (level 2) and then a paragraph opening with a large initial R. No running head. Margins hold no notes. A catchword sits at the lower right below the last line. Page number at the head.

main_text.p: fustentans paulatim conjungebat secum contetiosos adversarios, nec non placide singulos compellavit oratione Graeca; alios oratione co-ciliabat sibi, alios deterrebat, col-laudatis auctoribus utilis sententiae. Non destitit illos ad concordia ur-gere, donec universos a disceptatio-nibus, in eiusdem sententiae ac do-gmatis unitatem abduceret. Apud Eusebium lib. 4. cap. 37 porro haec habentur de Constantino. Quae ab episcopis in publicis conventibus editae erant regulae, sua consignabat & confirmabat auctoritate, ne reliquarum gentium principibus liceret, quae ab eis decreta essent, abrogare. Plura vide supr. quaest. de concilio Tridentino, pag. 82. 84. et in Medulla papistica pag. 231.
Testimonia pontificiorum pete ex dicta quaestione de auctoritate concilii Tridentini pag. 86. & seq.
main_text.head: Refutatio argumentationum pontificiarum.
main_text.p: Romanenses obiiciunt: Auctori-tatem regalem tantum controversiis

page.notes: Catchword at lower right reads as "sumpsit" but is only partly legible; marked [?]. The first line of the scan is shown with a fragment at the start of the page ("fustentans"), kept as a fragment. The paragraph ends on an unfinished sentence and continues on the next page. Text at the left edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Spelling "contetiosos" is as printed on the scan and may be a printing error for "contentiosos".
